simple: a collection of libraries and tools for writing robot software as many small programs that talk to each other.
analogy: the club's way of working: boards, desk, errands.
precise: the Robot Operating System version 2, an open-source robotics middleware framework and tool set; despite the name it is not an operating system but runs on one (Linux, among others), providing client libraries (for C++, rclcpp; for Python, rclpy), a communication layer built on DDS, and command-line tools.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one part of the robot's software with one job, such as "drive the wheels" or "read the laser".
analogy: one club member with a role.
precise: a participant in the ROS 2 graph, created through a client library, that owns publishers, subscriptions, service servers and clients, action servers and clients, timers and parameters; several nodes may live in one operating-system process.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named channel of messages of one type, such as "cmd_vel" carrying speed commands.
analogy: one notice board with a label.
precise: a named bus for anonymous, asynchronous publish–subscribe communication of messages of a single interface type; publishers and subscribers do not know of each other, and there may be any number of each.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: senders post messages under a name; whoever is interested in that name receives a copy.
analogy: pinning a note; reading the board.
precise: a messaging pattern in which producers (publishers) send data to a named topic without addressing receivers, and consumers (subscribers) register interest in the topic; the middleware matches them and delivers.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the agreed layout of a message: which fields, of which types.
analogy: the club's printed form for a route note.
precise: a ROS 2 interface definition (in a .msg file for messages, .srv for services, .action for actions) from which code for each client library is generated; a topic carries exactly one message type.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a question that one node asks another and gets one answer to.
analogy: Lena asking Tomás at the desk.
precise: remote-procedure-call style communication: a client sends a request message to a named service, one server processes it and returns a response message; intended for quick operations.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a long task you ask for, with progress reports on the way and a final result, which you may cancel.
analogy: the van's errand with phone calls.
precise: a long-running goal-oriented interaction with three parts (goal, feedback, result) and the ability to cancel; in ROS 2 it is built from services and topics underneath.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the picture of all running nodes and the topics, services and actions that connect them.
analogy: the club's whole web of boards and desks on a Saturday.
precise: the network of ROS 2 entities processing data together at a given time: nodes as vertices, communication endpoints matched by name and type as edges.
source: D1 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages "Nodes", "Topics", "Services", "Actions", "Interfaces" and the beginner command-line tutorials) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a prefix such as /robot1 that keeps the names of two robots apart, and the rules that turn a short name into a full one.
analogy: two clubs in the same hall, each with its own "route" board.
precise: names are hierarchical; a name starting with / is absolute, a name without it is relative and is prefixed by the node's namespace, and a name starting with ~ is private to the node; the fully resolved name is what endpoints are matched on.
source: D2 of F9-37 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 design articles: "Topic and Service name mapping to DDS" and "Actions") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the C++ library you use to write ROS 2 nodes.
analogy: the club's rule book and forms, in C++.
precise: the ROS 2 client library for C++; it provides the node class, publishers, subscriptions, services, actions (through a companion library), timers, parameters, logging and executors, built on a common C layer (rcl) and the middleware interface (rmw).
source: D1 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: tutorials "Creating a workspace", "Creating a package", "Writing a simple publisher and subscriber (C++)", "Using colcon to build packages", and the Concepts pages on intra-process communication and composition) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an alarm that calls your function again and again at a fixed period.
analogy: the club's bell every half hour.
precise: an entity created by a node with a period and a callback; when the period elapses, the timer becomes ready and an executor runs its callback; a wall timer measures time with the system's steady clock, other timers can follow the ROS clock (simulated time, F9-44).
source: D2 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, rclcpp API documentation (classes Node, Publisher, Subscription, TimerBase, executors, logging)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: handing your program's thread to ROS 2 so that it can call your callbacks whenever something is ready.
analogy: sitting by the pigeonhole and reading each note as it arrives.
precise: running an executor's loop, which waits for ready entities (timers, subscriptions with messages, service requests) and executes their callbacks, until shutdown (F9-39).
source: D2 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, rclcpp API documentation (classes Node, Publisher, Subscription, TimerBase, executors, logging)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a publisher, subscription or timer exists only as long as some part of your program keeps a pointer to it.
analogy: the card in Sipho's wallet.
precise: rclcpp returns entities as std::shared_ptr; when the last shared pointer is destroyed, the entity is destroyed and its callbacks no longer run; holding the pointers as node members ties the entities' lifetime to the node.
source: D2 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, rclcpp API documentation (classes Node, Publisher, Subscription, TimerBase, executors, logging)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a pointer that can look at an object without keeping it alive.
analogy: the secretary's list of members: having your name on the list does not keep you in the club.
precise: std::weak_ptr observes an object owned by std::shared_ptrs without contributing to its reference count; lock() returns a shared pointer if the object still exists, an empty one otherwise.
source: D3 of F9-38 (Bjarne Stroustrup, "A Tour of C++" (edition to be recorded), the chapters on resource management and smart pointers (shared_ptr, weak_ptr) and on lambda expressions) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a folder with your node's code plus two small files that say how to build it and what it needs.
analogy: a labelled toolbox with a packing list.
precise: the unit of building and release in ROS 2: a directory with a package manifest (package.xml) declaring name, version, licence and dependencies, and a build description (for C++, a CMakeLists.txt using ament's CMake functions).
source: D1 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: tutorials "Creating a workspace", "Creating a package", "Writing a simple publisher and subscriber (C++)", "Using colcon to build packages", and the Concepts pages on intra-process communication and composition) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a folder that holds several packages, and the tool that builds them all in the right order.
analogy: the club's workshop where all toolboxes are packed in order.
precise: a workspace is a directory with a source folder of packages; colcon is the ROS 2 build tool that discovers the packages, orders them by dependencies, builds each with its own build system, and produces a setup script that makes the results available to the shell.
source: D1 of F9-38 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: tutorials "Creating a workspace", "Creating a package", "Writing a simple publisher and subscriber (C++)", "Using colcon to build packages", and the Concepts pages on intra-process communication and composition) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of ROS 2 that decides which of your callbacks to run next, and runs it.
analogy: the club's helpers taking the next waiting job.
precise: an object to which nodes are added; when spun, it waits until timers, subscriptions, service servers and clients or other waitables are ready, and executes their callbacks on its thread (single-threaded executor) or on a pool of threads (multi-threaded executor), subject to callback groups.
source: D1 of F9-39 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Executors" and the how-to guide "Using Callback Groups") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a callback has something to do: its timer is due, or a message or request has arrived.
analogy: a job card waiting on the desk.
precise: an entity whose underlying wait condition is satisfied, so that the executor may take and execute its work.
source: D1 of F9-39 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Executors" and the how-to guide "Using Callback Groups") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a label you put on callbacks that tells the executor which of them may run at the same time.
analogy: which jobs share one notebook and pencil.
precise: a set of a node's callbacks with a type: in a mutually exclusive group at most one callback of the group executes at any time; in a reentrant group callbacks (including several instances of the same one) may execute in parallel; callbacks in different groups may always execute in parallel on a multi-threaded executor.
source: D1 of F9-39 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Executors" and the how-to guide "Using Callback Groups") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how long a callback was ready before a thread started it.
analogy: how long a pace call was overdue.
precise: start time minus ready time; in this chapter's model "wait" in the summary tables; one part of end-to-end latency (F9-43 measures the rest).
source: R1 of F9-39 (lab run in this build)

simple: a timer tick that never got its own run because the previous one had not run yet.
analogy: a pace call that was skipped because the previous one was still overdue.
precise: in this chapter's model, a deadline that arrives while the timer's previous instance is still waiting or running; it is counted and dropped, not queued. How rclcpp handles overdue timers must be checked (unverified box).
source: R1 of F9-39 (lab run in this build)

simple: a standard for programs to share data by topic name, with rules about how reliably and how long the data is kept.
analogy: the postal service behind the notice boards.
precise: an Object Management Group specification of a data-centric publish–subscribe middleware: applications in a domain read and write typed data samples on topics through data readers and data writers, with quality-of-service policies governing delivery, and with discovery of peers built in.
source: D2 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the data-centric publish–subscribe model, domains and participants, data writers and readers, history and reliability) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the agreed format and rules of the messages DDS sends over the network, so that DDS products from different makers understand each other.
analogy: the post office's rules for envelopes, numbering and receipts.
precise: the wire protocol defined by the OMG specification "DDS Interoperability Wire Protocol" (DDSI-RTPS): messages made of submessages carried over a transport such as UDP/IP, entities identified by GUIDs, a discovery protocol, and best-effort and reliable protocols between writers and readers.
source: D3 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "DDS Interoperability Wire Protocol (DDSI-RTPS)" specification, version 2.5 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): structure of the RTPS message, behaviour module (best-effort and reliable writers and readers), discovery module, mapping to UDP/IP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a numbered "world"; programs only find each other if they use the same number.
analogy: a town with its own post office; letters never cross towns.
precise: a DDS domain is a communication plane identified by an integer domain ID; only participants in the same domain discover each other and exchange data; in RTPS the domain ID also selects the network ports used.
source: D2 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the data-centric publish–subscribe model, domains and participants, data writers and readers, history and reliability) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one program's (or one ROS 2 context's) membership in a domain.
analogy: one branch of the club, registered at the post office.
precise: the DDS entity that represents an application's presence in a domain; it owns publishers, subscribers, topics, data writers and data readers, and is the unit of participant discovery.
source: D2 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the data-centric publish–subscribe model, domains and participants, data writers and readers, history and reliability) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the sending and receiving ends of one topic inside DDS.
analogy: Amara's numbered note pad and Kenji's pigeonhole.
precise: typed endpoints for one topic: a data writer publishes samples of the topic's type and keeps a history cache of them; a data reader receives samples into its own history cache and gives them to the application; writers and readers are matched by topic name, type and QoS compatibility.
source: D2 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the data-centric publish–subscribe model, domains and participants, data writers and readers, history and reliability) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how DDS programs find each other without a central list.
analogy: the opening letter to every address in town, and the replies.
precise: in RTPS, a two-stage process: a participant discovery protocol, in which participants periodically announce themselves (typically by multicast), followed by an endpoint discovery protocol, in which participants that know each other exchange descriptions of their writers and readers (topic, type, QoS) reliably; matching follows.
source: D3 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "DDS Interoperability Wire Protocol (DDSI-RTPS)" specification, version 2.5 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): structure of the RTPS message, behaviour module (best-effort and reliable writers and readers), discovery module, mapping to UDP/IP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number a writer puts on each sample, 1, 2, 3…
analogy: the number on each of Amara's notes.
precise: a writer-assigned, strictly increasing number identifying each change in the writer's history; readers use it to detect loss, order samples and request repairs.
source: D3 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "DDS Interoperability Wire Protocol (DDSI-RTPS)" specification, version 2.5 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): structure of the RTPS message, behaviour module (best-effort and reliable writers and readers), discovery module, mapping to UDP/IP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "I have sent 1 to 8", "I am missing 3", and "3 will never come".
analogy: Amara's postcard, Kenji's reply, and "that one is gone".
precise: RTPS submessages of the reliable protocol: a HEARTBEAT announces the range of sequence numbers available in the writer's history; an ACKNACK from a reader acknowledges what it has and lists what it is missing; a GAP tells a reader that a range of sequence numbers is not available and should not be waited for.
source: D3 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "DDS Interoperability Wire Protocol (DDSI-RTPS)" specification, version 2.5 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): structure of the RTPS message, behaviour module (best-effort and reliable writers and readers), discovery module, mapping to UDP/IP) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the plug that lets ROS 2 use DDS products from different makers.
analogy: the club's standard way of handing letters to whichever post company it uses.
precise: the ROS 2 abstraction layer (a C API) between the client libraries' common layer (rcl) and a middleware implementation; each supported DDS (or other) implementation provides an rmw implementation, chosen at run time.
source: D1 of F9-40 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts pages on the ROS 2 middleware ("About different ROS 2 DDS/RTPS vendors", "About internal ROS 2 interfaces") and "About Domain ID") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rules for turning a message's fields into a row of bytes.
analogy: how to fill in the post office's form, field by field.
precise: a binary serialisation format used by DDS for data samples, defining byte order and the alignment of primitive types; DDS's extensible-types specification defines versions of it.
source: D2 of F9-40 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the data-centric publish–subscribe model, domains and participants, data writers and readers, history and reliability) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a setting that says how a topic's messages should be delivered and kept.
analogy: the service you tick on the post-office form.
precise: in DDS, a named, typed setting attached to an entity (participant, topic, data writer, data reader…) that controls an aspect of its behaviour; ROS 2 exposes a subset of the DDS policies for publishers, subscriptions, services and actions.
source: D1 of F9-41 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Quality of Service settings" (policies, profiles, compatibility tables, QoS events) and the rclcpp API documentation of QoS classes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ready-made set of QoS settings for a typical kind of data.
analogy: the post office's "parcel" or "postcard" package.
precise: a named combination of policy values (for example a default profile and a sensor-data profile in ROS 2) used when creating an endpoint, from which individual policies may be changed.
source: D1 of F9-41 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Quality of Service settings" (policies, profiles, compatibility tables, QoS events) and the rclcpp API documentation of QoS classes) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whether lost messages are sent again.
analogy: registered post versus ordinary post.
precise: BEST_EFFORT: samples are sent once and may be lost; RELIABLE: the writer repairs losses for samples still in its history (F9-40).
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: whether old messages are kept for subscribers that join later.
analogy: whether the post office keeps a copy for latecomers.
precise: VOLATILE: no samples are kept for late-joining readers; TRANSIENT_LOCAL: the writer keeps its history and delivers it to readers that match later (DDS also defines TRANSIENT and PERSISTENT, which ROS 2 does not use by default).
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many recent messages are kept in a queue.
analogy: how many copies the sender keeps in the drawer.
precise: KEEP_LAST with a depth n keeps the newest n samples per instance and drops older ones; KEEP_ALL keeps all samples, up to resource limits.
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the longest allowed time between two messages.
analogy: "I promise a new route note at least every week."
precise: a period within which a new sample is expected; a writer offers a deadline it commits to meet, a reader requests one; if no sample arrives within the period, a "deadline missed" event is raised on that side.
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how a subscriber can tell that a publisher is still alive, even when it has nothing to say.
analogy: a sender's regular "still here" postcard.
precise: a policy (AUTOMATIC, or MANUAL_BY_TOPIC, where the application must assert it) with a lease duration; if the writer does not assert liveliness within the lease, readers see it as not alive.
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how long a message stays valid before it is thrown away undelivered.
analogy: a "use by" date on a note.
precise: the maximum time between publication and delivery; samples older than this are removed from caches and not delivered.
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the rule that a subscriber may not ask for more than the publisher offers.
analogy: the clerk comparing Rafael's and Ines's cards.
precise: for policies marked request/offered in DDS, a data writer's offered value must be at least as strong as the data reader's requested value; otherwise the two are not matched and both sides receive an "incompatible QoS" status.
source: D2 of F9-41 (Object Management Group, "Data Distribution Service (DDS)" specification, version 1.4 (shown as latest in the guide's registry): the section on supported QoS policies, with the table of policies, their request/offered (RxO) property and changeability, and the sections on RELIABILITY, DURABILITY, HISTORY, DEADLINE, LIVELINESS and LIFESPAN) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a named setting of a node, such as a wheel's radius, that you can change without recompiling.
analogy: the saddle height on a member's card.
precise: a named, typed value owned by a node; a node declares the parameters it accepts (with defaults and optional descriptors such as ranges), values can be set at start-up from the command line, launch files or parameter files, and at run time through services, subject to the node's validation callback.
source: D1 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Parameters" and the tutorials "Understanding parameters" and "Using parameters in a class (C++)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a text file with the settings of one or more nodes.
analogy: the stack of members' cards.
precise: a YAML file that maps node names to parameter names and values, passed to nodes at start-up; values for parameters a node has not declared are not applied (unless the node allows undeclared parameters).
source: D1 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts page "Parameters" and the tutorials "Understanding parameters" and "Using parameters in a class (C++)") — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a file that starts a whole set of nodes with their settings in one command.
analogy: the ride leader's checklist.
precise: a description, written in Python, XML or YAML, of the processes to start (nodes with package, executable, name, namespace, parameters, remappings), plus arguments, conditions and event handlers; the ROS 2 launch system executes it.
source: D2 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: the "Launch" tutorials (creating launch files; using substitutions and event handlers; managing large projects) and the remapping section of the command-line arguments design article) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: renaming a topic or service from outside a node when you start it.
analogy: telling Felix "your 'route' board today is the one in the hall".
precise: a rule given at start-up that replaces a name the node uses with another name before resolution (F9-37), so that nodes written independently can be connected without changing their code.
source: D2 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: the "Launch" tutorials (creating launch files; using substitutions and event handlers; managing large projects) and the remapping section of the command-line arguments design article) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a node that starts in a "not ready" state and only begins working when told to, step by step.
analogy: a bicycle that goes from "checked" to "at the start line" to "riding".
precise: a ROS 2 node with a standard state machine (primary states Unconfigured, Inactive, Active, Finalized) whose transitions (configure, activate, deactivate, cleanup, shutdown) are requested from outside and executed through callbacks the node implements; publishers of a lifecycle node publish only in the Active state.
source: D3 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 design article "Managed nodes" and the rclcpp_lifecycle API documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one step from one state to the next, which can succeed or fail.
analogy: "check the bike", "go to the start line".
precise: a named change between primary states; while it runs, the node is in an intermediate transition state, the node's callback decides success or failure, and an error leads to error processing.
source: D3 of F9-42 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 design article "Managed nodes" and the rclcpp_lifecycle API documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a file holding a recording of messages from chosen topics, with their times.
analogy: a photocopy of every notice pinned during the ride, each with its pin time.
precise: a ROS 2 recording made by the rosbag2 tool: for each recorded topic, its name, type and QoS, and for each message its serialised data and a receive time stamp, stored through a storage plugin (for example an SQLite or MCAP file) with a metadata file.
source: D1 of F9-43 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: tutorial "Recording and playing back data" and the rosbag2 project documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how fast a recording is played back compared with real time.
analogy: pinning the photocopies again twice as fast.
precise: the factor by which the replay tool compresses the intervals between recorded messages; at rate 2.0, messages recorded 100 ms apart are published 50 ms apart.
source: D1 of F9-43 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: tutorial "Recording and playing back data" and the rosbag2 project documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time written inside a message saying when its data was measured.
analogy: the time printed on the notice, not the time you read it.
precise: the stamp field of a message's std_msgs/Header, set by the producer to the acquisition time of the data; it travels with the message, so it is unchanged by transport delay, recording or replay.
source: D2 of F9-43 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts "Clock and time" (ROS time, simulation time) and the message definition of std_msgs/Header) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: recording tiny time-stamped events inside the running programs, such as "callback started", to measure where time goes.
analogy: a stopwatch log of when each helper picked up and finished each job.
precise: low-overhead instrumentation of ROS 2 and the application with tracepoints, collected by a tracer (LTTng on Linux in the ros2_tracing project) and analysed offline to obtain callback durations, latencies and message flow.
source: D3 of F9-43 (C. Bédard, I. Lütkebohle and M. Dagenais, "ros2_tracing: Multipurpose Low-Overhead Framework for Real-Time Tracing of ROS 2", IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2022; and the ros2_tracing project documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that draws what the robot thinks: its position, sensor readings and plans, in 3D.
analogy: a map on the club-house wall with everyone's position pinned to it.
precise: RViz (RViz2 in ROS 2) subscribes to topics such as laser scans, point clouds, odometry, transforms and markers and renders them in a common coordinate frame; it shows data, it does not simulate.
source: D4 of F9-43 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, RViz user guide in the ROS 2 documentation) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a program that pretends to be the robot's body and the world around it, so that the robot's software can run without hardware.
analogy: the turbo trainer and its screen.
precise: software that integrates rigid-body dynamics (and contacts, friction, joints) in time steps, models sensors by computing what they would measure in the simulated world, models actuators, and exchanges commands and sensor data with the robot software through the same interfaces as the hardware.
source: D1 of F9-44 (Open Robotics, Gazebo documentation (Gazebo Sim, current releases): getting started, SDF worlds, physics and sensors, and the SDFormat specification) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the small amount of pretend time the simulator moves forward each time it computes the world.
analogy: one frame of the trainer's video.
precise: the fixed time increment of the simulator's numerical integration; smaller steps give more accurate and more stable contacts at more computation per simulated second.
source: D1 of F9-44 (Open Robotics, Gazebo documentation (Gazebo Sim, current releases): getting started, SDF worlds, physics and sensors, and the SDFormat specification) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how fast simulated time passes compared with real time.
analogy: the video playing at half speed on a slow laptop.
precise: simulated seconds advanced per wall-clock second; 1.0 means real time, below 1 means the simulator cannot keep up (or is slowed on purpose), above 1 means faster than real time.
source: D1 of F9-44 (Open Robotics, Gazebo documentation (Gazebo Sim, current releases): getting started, SDF worlds, physics and sensors, and the SDFormat specification) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the simulator's own clock, which the robot's programs read instead of the wall clock.
analogy: the clock in the video, not the one on the wall.
precise: a time source published by the simulator (in ROS 2 on a clock topic) that nodes configured for simulation time use for their timers, time stamps and durations, so that their behaviour is the same at any real-time factor.
source: D2 of F9-44 (Open Robotics and the ROS 2 community, ROS 2 documentation: Concepts "Clock and time" (simulation time, the clock topic)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the true position of the robot, which a simulator knows exactly and a real robot never does.
analogy: the trainer software knowing exactly where you are on the virtual road.
precise: the simulator's internal state of the robot's pose and velocity, used to measure the error of the robot's own estimates (odometry, EKF); on hardware it can only be approximated by an external measurement system.
source: R1 of F9-44 (lab run in this build)

simple: the description of everything in the simulation: floor, walls, objects, light, gravity and the robot.
analogy: the road and the scenery on the trainer's screen.
precise: a file (in Gazebo, an SDF file) listing models with their geometry, mass, inertia, joints, sensors and plugins, and world properties such as gravity and the physics engine's step size.
source: D1 of F9-44 (Open Robotics, Gazebo documentation (Gazebo Sim, current releases): getting started, SDF worlds, physics and sensors, and the SDFormat specification) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
